new_entities.name: Mandibular advancement device for mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea
aliases: MAD for mild to moderate OSA
oral appliance for mild to moderate sleep apnea
new_entities.description: Custom or adjustable mandibular advancement oral appliances used to treat adults with mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Apnea-hypopnea index
new_entities.description: The apnea-hypopnea index, representing the number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep.

edges.effect_quant: Mandibular advancement devices usually improve but do not normalize OSA severity. A 2025 meta-analysis in East Asian patients found pooled AHI reduction of 19.1 events/h, and randomized trials in mostly mild to moderate disease report response rates around 52% to 54%.
edges.population: adults with mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea, especially those refusing or not tolerating CPAP
edges.mechanism: Advancing the mandible enlarges and stabilizes the retrolingual airway, reducing upper-airway collapse during sleep.
edges.summary: This is a real therapeutic edge, particularly for mild to moderate OSA and for patients who value a non-PAP option. The average effect is meaningful but generally smaller than CPAP.
edges.caveats: Response is heterogeneous and complete normalization is uncommon. Effectiveness depends on dentition, craniofacial anatomy, device titration, and adherence, and some devices trade efficacy for comfort or convenience.

evidence.citation: YongCW et al 2025 J Clin Sleep Med
